label: TP
reason: Alert 1 (java/insecure-randomness): alert-TP — resolved sink value is rememberMeKey, which equals Float.toString(new java.util.Random().nextFloat()).substring(2). java.util.Random is a predictable PRNG, and rememberMeKey is used as a cookie value for authentication/session persistence (stored in session at line 100 and sent as HttpOnly+Secure cookie at line 101). Weak randomness feeding security-sensitive material (auth token/cookie) constitutes a real vulnerability. Alert 2 (java/xss): alert-FP — resolved sink values are rememberMe.getName() = "rememberMe" + testCaseNumber (server-derived from class name, not user input) and rememberMe.getValue() = rememberMeKey (derived from java.util.Random, not user-controlled). Neither source flows from user-provided data; the cookie is freshly created in the else branch with server-generated values. Case TP: driven by Alert 1 (insecure randomness used for security-sensitive remember-me cookie).

evidence.note: java.util.Random().nextFloat() used to generate rememberMeKey — insecure PRNG for security-sensitive token
rememberMeKey used as cookie value and stored in session — security-sensitive material fed by weak randomness
